transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess what made me finally say something is my eating’s been kind of off the last few weeks. Like, I’ll accidentally skip breakfast and lunch, and then even at dinner I just sort of pick at it, even when my wife made something. She gets annoyed because, you know, she put effort into it. And I noticed my jeans are feeling looser, which… I mean, normally I wouldn’t come in just for that, but it’s been weird.
Have you been trying to lose weight?

No, not really. I mean, I’ve thought about getting in better shape before—like everybody does, I guess—but this isn’t that. I’m not dieting or counting calories or anything. I just keep skipping breakfast and lunch without really meaning to, and then at dinner I’m kind of just moving food around the plate even if my wife cooked. My jeans are starting to feel loose, so that’s what made me notice it.
Are you happy about the weight loss you've experienced?

Not really happy, no. I mean, I guess loose jeans sounds nice in theory, like when you find an old pair in the closet and they fit again, but this doesn’t feel like that. It’s more like I just keep forgetting to eat—breakfast and lunch especially—and then at dinner I’m sort of pushing food around, even when my wife made something good. So the weight part is more something I noticed because my clothes feel different, not something I’m trying for.
Have you noticed any changes in your interest in the things you usually enjoy doing?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I still kind of do the usual stuff when it’s in front of me, but I haven’t really sat down and thought, like, “Am I enjoying this less?” My wife would probably have a better read on that than me—she notices things before I do. Like with the jeans thing, I didn’t even really notice until they started feeling weird around the waist.

So… I don’t know. I can’t say I’ve clearly noticed a change there.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Yeah… I think so. Most days lately I wake up and there’s this kind of heavy, flat feeling there, like before anything even happens. The apartment feels really quiet in the morning, which is weird because it’s always been quiet, you know? Like the fridge humming and cars outside, same as always, but it just feels… heavier.

I’ll pick up my guitar sometimes, because that used to kind of shift my mood a little, even if I was just messing around, but lately it doesn’t really lift me much. I’ll sit there with it and then kind of just put it back down. So, yeah, sad or down… I guess that’s probably the word for it.
How much weight would you say you've lost since you first noticed the change in your eating habits?

I haven’t actually weighed myself, so I don’t have a number. It’s more that my jeans are starting to feel loose, which is what made me notice it. For the past few weeks I’ve been skipping breakfast and lunch without really meaning to, and then at dinner I just kind of pick at whatever my wife made. So… I can’t say pounds, exactly.
Would you say the looseness of your jeans is noticeable to others, or is it something only you've noticed?

I think it’s mostly something I’ve noticed, maybe my wife might’ve noticed but she hasn’t said it outright. It’s not like they’re falling off me or anything. It’s just when I put them on, they don’t sit the same, and that’s what made me think about it.

The bigger thing is my eating’s been weird the last few weeks. I’ll just skip breakfast and lunch without really planning to, and then dinner comes around and even if my wife made something, I kind of pick at it. So the jeans feeling loose is what tipped me off, I guess.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

I haven’t really thought about it like that. I mean, I don’t think I’m sitting there worrying about gaining weight or checking calories or anything… it’s more just, I notice my clothes feel different and then my mind wanders. Like I’ll remember these old jeans I had in college that never fit right, and—sorry, that’s not really the point.

I guess I’m not sure. It doesn’t feel like fear of weight gain is the main thing, but I haven’t really paid close attention to that specifically.
Are you afraid of gaining weight back after this unintentional weight loss?

I don’t know that I’m afraid of gaining it back, exactly. I mean, “back” is funny because I don’t even know how much I lost in the first place. I just noticed the jeans thing.

I guess if they got tight again I might feel annoyed, but that’s more like… clothes are expensive, and I hate shopping for jeans because the sizes never make sense. But no, I don’t think I’m worried about gaining weight back in that way. At least not that I’ve noticed.
Are you afraid of gaining weight in general?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think I walk around afraid of gaining weight in general. Like, I’m not avoiding scales or… well, I guess I don’t really use a scale much anyway, so that’s not a great example.

It’s more that I notice little things, like how clothes fit, and then I overthink it for a bit. But if you’re asking whether gaining weight is something I’m scared of day to day, I don’t think so. At least it doesn’t feel like that’s what’s going on.
Do you think you would be upset if you gained back the weight you lost?

Maybe a little upset, but I don’t think that’s what’s been bothering me most. What made me mention it is more that my eating’s been weird the last few weeks. I’ll just kind of miss breakfast and lunch without really deciding to, and then at dinner I’m picking at food even if my wife made something.

And then I noticed my jeans are looser, which is what made me think about the weight thing. But it’s not like I’m trying to keep it off or I’d panic if it came back. It’s more just… it caught my attention.
Do you ever feel like you're eating in response to emotions, rather than just being hungry?

I don’t think it’s emotions exactly. Or… I mean, maybe sometimes, like anybody, if I’m stressed I’ll snack, but that’s not really what I was trying to describe.

What made me bring it up is more that my eating’s just been off the last few weeks. I’ll skip breakfast and lunch without meaning to, and then by dinner my wife will have cooked something and I’m just sort of picking at it. Which makes me feel bad, because she notices, and then I’m like, “No, it’s good, I’m just not hungry,” and then it turns into a whole thing.

And then I noticed my jeans getting loose, so that’s what caught my attention. Not really eating because I’m sad or mad or something. More like I’m just not eating much without planning to.
Do you think you would feel better about yourself if you were thinner

I don’t know… I don’t really think of it that way. Like, I don’t look in the mirror and think, “If I were thinner, everything would be better.”

I mean, clothes fitting differently can make me notice it, and then I’ll get kind of stuck thinking about it for a minute. But feeling better about myself? I’m not sure that’s connected. Honestly, half the time I’m more focused on whether I even remembered to eat, or whether my wife is going to ask why I barely touched dinner, and then I’m explaining myself and it gets awkward.

So… no, I don’t think being thinner would make me feel better about myself. Or at least that’s not something I’ve noticed.
Do you think your eating habits have changed because you're trying to avoid gaining weight?

No, I don’t think I’m doing it to avoid gaining weight. It’s more like… I’ll realize later that I just didn’t eat. Like I’ll skip breakfast, then lunch kind of disappears too, and I didn’t really make a decision about it.

Then dinner comes around and my wife made something, and I’m sitting there sort of picking at it, and I feel bad because she can tell. And then I noticed my jeans were looser, which is why I brought it up. But it’s not like I’m thinking, “Don’t gain weight.” It’s more just my appetite’s been off the last few weeks.
Do you think your change in eating habits is related to a fear of gaining weight?

No, I don’t think it’s fear of gaining weight. I mean, I guess everybody has moments where they don’t love how their clothes fit or whatever, but that’s not what this feels like.

It’s more that the last few weeks my eating’s been weird. I’ll kind of accidentally skip breakfast, and then lunch too, and suddenly it’s dinner. My wife will have cooked something and I’ll just be picking at it, which makes me feel bad because she put effort into it. And then my jeans started feeling loose, so I noticed it more.

But I’m not trying to lose weight or avoid gaining it. It’s just like my appetite is off.
Do you think you would like to lose more weight?

No… I mean, not really. I don’t have like a goal weight in my head or anything.

The thing that made me mention it was just that my eating’s been off the last few weeks. I’ll skip breakfast without really meaning to, and then somehow lunch doesn’t happen either, and by dinner my wife has cooked and I’m just kind of moving food around or picking at it. Which feels bad, because she notices, and then I feel like I’m making it into a thing.

And then my jeans started feeling loose, so I noticed that too. But I’m not sitting there thinking, “I want to lose more weight.” It’s more like… I’m not eating much and I don’t totally know why.
Do you think you would be deliberately eating less if you weren't losing weight?

I don’t think I’d be deliberately eating less, no. It’s not really deliberate now, honestly.

It’s more like… I’ll look up and realize I skipped breakfast, and then lunch somehow didn’t happen either. And by dinner my wife’s made something, and I’m just kind of picking at it. Which feels bad, because she notices, and then I start feeling awkward about it.

The loose jeans were just what made me notice it more. Like, I wasn’t aiming for that. My appetite’s just been off the past few weeks.
Do you think your mood affects how much you eat?

Yeah, I think it probably does, at least lately. Like, when I’m feeling off, eating just kind of drops out of the day.

I’ll skip breakfast without meaning to, then suddenly it’s later and I realize I didn’t eat lunch either. Then at dinner my wife has cooked, and I’m just picking at it, which makes me feel kind of guilty. We’ve got these plates she likes—actually she got them from her sister, I think—and I’ll be sitting there moving food around like a kid, which is embarrassing.

So yeah, my mood seems tied to it somehow. My appetite’s just been weird the past few weeks, and my jeans are starting to feel loose.
Do you think there's something on your mind that's causing you to not feel like eating?

I don’t know if it’s one specific thing on my mind. I keep trying to figure that out, actually, and then I start thinking about other stuff, like whether I’ve been making dinner weird for my wife.

What made me bring it up is more that my eating’s been off the past few weeks. I’ll skip breakfast without really meaning to, and then lunch just sort of doesn’t happen. Then by dinner, even if my wife cooked, I’m just picking at it. And then my jeans started feeling loose, so it made me notice it more.

So… maybe something’s affecting it, but I can’t point to one thing.
Do you think you would be eating more if you weren't losing weight?

Maybe? I mean, I’m not trying to eat less because I’m losing weight, if that makes sense. It’s more that my eating got weird first, and then I noticed my jeans were loose.

Like the last few weeks I’ll just skip breakfast without meaning to, and then lunch kind of disappears too. Dinner is the only one that’s obvious because my wife cooked, and I’m sitting there picking at it, which feels… rude, I guess. She has this one meal she makes that I usually like, and even that I’m kind of just pushing around.

So yeah, if my appetite was normal I’d probably be eating more. The weight thing is just what made me realize it was happening.
